entries.reasoning:
This statement came from the repository's local Git history, not from the Azure DevOps story.

Evidence used:

 git log --all --oneline -S "IsContentAssignmentUpdated" -- Data/Aveva.EI.Repositories/CanvasDrawingsRepository.cs Presentation/Aveva.EI.CanvasDrawings/SGCClient/CanvasEventManager.cs

This identified commit 56f69e11583, titled Merged PR 921114: Termination drawing update and performance, related work item #4029829.

Then git blame -L 1037,1048 Presentation/Aveva.EI.CanvasDrawings/SGCClient/CanvasEventManager.cs showed that the activation-time content-assignment check was added in that commit. I also inspected git show 56f69e11583 -- ... and saw the repository history-checking method and drawing refresh path introduced together.

The precise conclusion is that Git history confirms this refresh mechanism was introduced as part of an earlier termination-drawing content-assignment feature and exists in the current branch. It does not prove that work item 3735081 is fully verified or that the existing implementation satisfies every scenario in that story.
entries.outcome: Recorded historical provenance separately from validation.
